- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is neutral or flat; true outcomes often show downward correction or slower rise.
- Underestimate spikes in later forecast windows; model tends to lag behind actual price surges, especially after 10–15 day horizons.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., 80+), leading to overcorrection in subsequent days — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast shows sustained upward trend beyond 10 days, reduce slope slightly to align with historical 30-day mean reversion.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model should not overreact to recent price volatility — suppress early forecast momentum unless confirmed by technical indicators.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — introduce slight downward bias in final 5–7 days if prior 10–15 days show no breakout.
